A 73-year-old man seeks medical attention due to worsening breathlessness over three months,
particularly noticeable during activities like walking and lawn mowing. He also experienced two
episodes of severe dizziness while moving furniture. His medical history includes hypertension,
diabetes mellitus, cluster headaches, and basal cell carcinoma. His vital signs show: temperature

98.3°F (36.8°C), blood pressure 137/88 mmHg, pulse 67/min, respirations 20/min, and oxygen
saturation 94% on room air. The physical examination reveals clear lungs and a 3/6 systolic ejection
murmur that is most prominent at the right second intercostal space. Both carotid pulses are noted to
be delayed and decreased in intensity. Which of the following conditions is most likely to be associated
with this patient's clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Peripheral arterial disease (B) Mitral valve
prolapse (C) Coronary artery calcification (D) Pulmonary hypertension (E) Cerebral artery aneurysm
(F) Deep vein thrombosis (G) Retinal hemorrhages (H) Renal artery stenosis (I) Erectile dysfunction (J)
Colonic angiodysplasia
 A. Coronary artery calcification
B. Erectile dysfunction
C. Colonic angiodysplasia
D. Retinal hemorrhages
E. Peripheral arterial disease
F. Cerebral artery aneurysm
G. Mitral valve prolapse
H. Renal artery stenosis
I. Pulmonary hypertension
